name: Capture or sabotage a structure
summary: The unit reaches an enemy building, turret or device and works on it in contact or from inside instead of destroying it. Depending on the version it takes the structure over for its own team, switches one of its functions off for a while (power, production, spawning, a countdown), robs it (money, the enemy's view, word of what they are building) or clamps on a device that shuts it down and slowly wrecks it. The work needs contact or a short reach and takes time; the RTS originals often use the unit up, and big or healthy structures may need damaging first. Defenders answer by guarding, detecting or killing the capturer, removing its device and taking the structure back. A neutral control point is a game-mode rule, and taking a neutral building is not this pattern: it needs an enemy one.
counterplay: Guard the structures that matter: anti-infantry fire, mines or a turret covering the way in, since capturers are usually fragile and often unarmed.
Bring detection: many capturers rely on stealth or a disguise to get close.
Interrupt the work: a hack or capture takes time and stops if the capturer dies or is pushed out of reach.
Knock planted devices off: an engineer or repair tool removes a sapper before it wrecks the structure.
Take it back: a captured structure can be recaptured or destroyed, and a sabotage wears off after a while.
Keep structures healthy: some captures only work on badly damaged buildings, so timely repair blocks them.
Spread key functions over several structures, so one sabotage doesn't switch everything off.

other_examples.note: Sent into an enemy building, the engineer is used up and either damages it heavily or, once the building is in poor shape, captures it; a building at full health can take several engineers, and turrets and other hardened defences generally can't be captured. Sent into a friendly building, it repairs it to full at once.

sources.title: Engineer (Red Alert 1), Command & Conquer Wiki
sources.note: Its quote box copies the Engineer paragraph of the Red Alert manual; capture rules are cited to EA's released game code.

other_examples.note: Entering an enemy building spends the spy and triggers that building's sabotage: a power plant blacks out the enemy base for a while, a radar building wipes the enemy's map, a refinery hands over a fifth of the enemy's money, a barracks or factory makes the spy's own new units veterans, a superweapon restarts its countdown, and a battle lab unlocks a special unit.

sources.title: Spy (Red Alert 2), Command & Conquer Wiki
sources.note: Its quote box copies the Spy paragraph of the Red Alert 2 manual, which says the effect depends on the building entered.

other_examples.note: Infiltration takes the enemy's radar offline while sharing their view, cuts power for a short time, steals money, stops every production building of the entered type, or switches off top-tier units, which makes top-tier aircraft crash. A superweapon's countdown restarts.

An unarmed hacker, stealthed except while she uses an ability, who takes over enemy (and neutral) buildings from a short distance, siphons money from supply buildings and shuts down vehicles. Every hack makes her visible, so her team has to cover her, and a careless base can be hacked from outside its walls.

A stealthed infiltrator that climbs cliffs and is used up when it gets into an enemy building. It does no damage but steals cash, switches production or power off for a short time, restarts the enemy's support-power and superweapon timers, and blows up fake buildings. Mines around buildings and units that detect stealth stop it.
The basic American soldier gains a capture order once its side buys the upgrade, and can then take over enemy facilities as well as neutral tech buildings.

sources.title: Ranger (Generals), Command & Conquer Wiki
sources.note: Its quote box copies the Ranger paragraph of the Generals manual.

other_examples.unit: Queen's infestation of a command center (Zerg)
other_examples.note: A Zerg queen can enter a badly damaged Terran command center and infest it; the building turns Zerg and from then on breeds suicide infantry for its new owner.

shooter_analogues.note: The Infiltrator walks up to an enemy terminal or base turret and holds the use key while a progress ring fills; the equipment then belongs to their faction and can be used at once. The hacker must stay close for the whole time but may look away. Every class can hack some base equipment, such as generators, and an implant lets defenders harden their own turrets so that attackers must hack them twice.

The Spy clamps a sapper onto an Engineer's sentry gun, dispenser or teleporter: it stops working straight away and loses health until it is destroyed, unless the Engineer knocks the sapper off with a few wrench hits. Sapping doesn't break the Spy's disguise, the Engineer gets a HUD alert, and a Spy can sap faster than one Engineer can repair, so the Spy must be dealt with too.

player_translation.summary: An infiltrator's objective tool: get next to, or inside, an enemy turret, spawn beacon or base structure and hold to turn it, switch it off or rob it. It lets sneaky players win without winning gunfights, and gives defenders a reason to guard, check and repair.
as_user: Pick a target: a turret or device an enemy player placed, a deployed spawn beacon, or one of the team structures the map provides (a generator, a supply depot, a terminal).
Hold Q at touching distance and a progress ring fills over the structure; you can't fire while you work and must stay close, so the approach and those few seconds are the risk.

What finishing does depends on the variant: take-over turns the structure to your team at its current health; switch-off stops one function for a fixed time (a turret stops firing, a beacon stops spawning, a depot stops paying); spy-inside shares what it sees or builds with your team.
Unlike the RTS original you are not used up: you walk away from the finished job and can do it again elsewhere.
With the break-then-take variant a healthy structure only takes damage from you; teammates must bring it low first.
as_target: You get a clear alarm: a 'structure under attack' message with a direction marker, a progress ring over the structure and a sound from it, so you have the length of the hack to respond.
You stop it by killing or shoving the capturer out of reach, by hitting the structure with a repair tool (which drains the progress), or by knocking a planted device off.
After a take-over your old turret shoots at you; retake it with your own capturer or destroy it.
A switch-off shows a countdown on the structure, so you know when it comes back.
teammates: Attackers escort or distract while the capturer works; a disguised or cloaked capturer reaches the target on its own.
Turning an enemy turret flips a fortified position in one move, so it is a natural opener for a push.
Spying inside a structure, or turning a spawn beacon off, tells the whole team where and when the enemy will gather.
Defenders keep a repair class near key structures: repairing in time blocks damage-first captures and clears devices.
controls: Move with WASD and aim with the mouse; left mouse fires your weapon, if any.
Hold Q (signature) on the enemy structure under the cursor while in reach: the ring fills; releasing or leaving reach stops it, and progress drains slowly, so a short interruption isn't a full reset.
Clamp-a-device variant: tap Q to stick a device on the structure, then you are free to fight or leave.
Defenders: the repair tool's main fire on a structure being worked on drains the progress or removes the device.
The pattern uses one counted key (Q), within any tier's budget.
feedback: A progress ring over the structure, coloured by the capturing team and visible to both teams from above.
An alarm and minimap ping for the owners, and a distinct sound loop at the structure while it is worked on.
A captured structure changes colour and flag at once, with a short 'captured' banner for both teams.
A switched-off structure sparks or goes dark and shows a countdown until it recovers.
Planted devices are large, team-coloured and blinking, so defenders can find and hit them.
changes_from_rts: RTS capturers are used up on entry; a player has to survive the action, so the price is the time spent exposed while working, not the unit.
Instant captures on contact leave no counterplay, so the hold takes a few seconds and shows the owners a ring and an alarm.

RTS bases are full of buildings; a team shooter has few enemy structures, so the targets are player-placed turrets and devices, spawn beacons and the map's team structures, and the generator should only offer the pattern where those exist.
Effects such as taking a fifth of the enemy's money or restarting a superweapon are swingy and invisible; they become short, visible, time-limited effects on one structure.
Taking a neutral point is a game-mode rule that every unit shares, not this pattern.
Recapture must always be possible, or one hack decides the match.

team_play.notes: The capturer needs cover while it works and the defenders need someone who guards, detects and repairs, so both teams organise around the structures. Spying inside one gives the team information; turning one opens a push.

notes: The maps or modes need enemy structures with an owner team that can change: player-placed turrets and devices, spawn beacons, and map structures.
Changing owner must update targeting, colours, minimap, spawn lists and income for every client at once.
A channelled action with progress, reach checks, slow decay and interruption, plus repair that drains progress or removes devices.
Each sabotage effect (turret off, spawning off, income off, view shared) is its own small system with a timer.
Taking a strong turret or a spawn point can swing a match; keep effects short or limited to small structures, and always allow recapture.
Chain-hacking a base while its defenders respawn; give each structure a short lock-out after it is retaken.
If a map has nothing to capture the pattern is dead weight, so the generator should only roll it for modes with structures.
Stealing money or the enemy's view is invisible to the victim and feels unfair; always tell the victim what was taken.
Both teams must see who owns each structure and which ones are being worked on.
A turret that changes sides needs an unmistakable flip cue, or players walk into fire from their own former turret.
A sabotage that quietly switches things off (power, spawning) needs a visible state on the structure.

variants.name: Take it over
variants.summary: Hold in contact to turn an enemy turret, device or building to your team; it keeps its health and works for you until it is retaken.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 1 Engineer, Generals Black Lotus and Rangers, PlanetSide 2 hacking

adds_strengths.why: Takes enemy turrets and structures over and keeps them working for its own team until they are retaken.

variants.name: Switch it off
variants.summary: Get inside or work on the structure to stop one of its functions for a fixed time: power, production, spawning or a team ability's countdown.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 2 and 3 spies, Zero Hour Saboteur

variants.name: Spy on it
variants.summary: Get inside to share what the structure knows with your team, such as the enemy's view or what it is producing; the structure keeps working for its owner.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 1 spy (Radar Dome, factories), Red Alert 3 spy (construction yard)

variants.name: Rob it
variants.summary: Move a share of the enemy team's money or charge from the structure into your team's, with a clear notice to the victims.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 2 and 3 spies, Black Lotus cash hack, Zero Hour Saboteur

variants.name: Clamp a device
variants.summary: Tap to stick a device on the structure: it stops working at once and loses health until the device is knocked off, and you are free to move.

adds_weaknesses.why: It must get close enough to stick the device on, and enemies can knock the device off.

variants.name: Break it, then take it
variants.summary: The capture only works once the structure is badly damaged; on a healthy one it only does damage, so teammates soften it first.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 1 Engineer, StarCraft queen infesting a command center

adds_strengths.why: Turns an enemy structure its team has worn down into its own and keeps it working for them until it is retaken.

variants.name: Hack from range
variants.summary: Works from a short distance, so you can stay behind cover or outside a fence, but starting the hack gives your position away.

adds_weaknesses.why: Starting the hack gives its position away, and it must stay in reach until the hack ends.

variants.name: Turn it into a nest
variants.summary: A captured structure starts producing small minions for your team until it is destroyed or retaken.

adds_strengths.why: Keeps the enemy structure it took over, which then adds a stream of small minions to its team's side.
Turns enemy turrets and structures to its own side, switches them off, robs them or spies through them, without having to destroy them.

adds_weaknesses.why: It has to reach the structure and stay next to it while the work runs, exposed and unable to shoot.

counters.why: Enemy turrets and devices can be turned or switched off instead of destroyed.
A deployed spawn point can be switched off or taken, cutting the enemy's way back to the front.

countered_by.why: Sustained fire around the structure kills the fragile capturer while it works.
Mines around key structures catch capturers on the way in.
Repairing the structure drains the capture and knocks planted devices off.

open_questions: Which enemy structures will Shamble Frontlines maps have (team bases, generators, spawn points, player-built turrets)? The pattern only works where there is something to capture.
Should a capture change the owner for good (until retaken) or only for a fixed time?
Should the capturer survive the action (the proposal here) or be used up as in the RTS, with a cheap respawn?

shooter_fit.reason: PlanetSide 2 hacking and the Team Fortress 2 sapper show it works with players, but it depends on maps having enemy structures worth taking, which a team shooter has far fewer of than an RTS base.

review.notes: Re-checked field by field against its sources by the batch r1 checker, which covered all 33 batch patterns; research/r1/checker/checks.json lists every field and verdict. Nothing was found wrong.
